title: Uniform and Letter
premise: Orsen Yarrow, a quiet chauffeur for suffragist Marguerite Hale, reads every letter that passes through their hands and keeps every secret they've learned. When a child named Ida is abandoned at the Hale house with a note demanding the face be forgotten, Orsen recognizes the handwriting of Anton Reiss, a German correspondent they promised in 1913 to help reach England. Now, with war declared and Anton branded enemy, Orsen must smuggle Ida to safety and honor a peacetime promise before the river freezes and the last crossings close. The novel ends with Orsen delivering Ida to Anton across the ice at great personal cost, returning to find Marguerite arrested, and choosing at last to stop being invisible by testifying on her behalf.
about_author: Paloma Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in provincial English collections. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'other.'

chapters.title: The Man Who Reads Other People's Mail
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishes Orsen's routine: driving Marguerite Hale to suffrage meetings, steaming open letters, memorizing secrets as insurance and habit. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being a person no one looks at.

chapters.title: A Parcel Left in the Rain
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A child, Ida, appears at the service door with a note in familiar handwriting: 'Forget the face. Keep the child. Burn this.' Orsen recognizes Anton Reiss's hand and hides the girl in the coach house. Beat: fear disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Marguerite's War Chest
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The movement pivots to wartime work; Marguerite suspects something is wrong with her driver. Orsen lies smoothly for the first time. Beat: the first crack in a relationship built on trust.

chapters.title: Letters from a Man Now Enemy
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback to 1913. Orsen and Anton corresponded about translating suffrage pamphlets; Orsen promised passage and shelter if Anton ever needed to flee. Beat: nostalgia curdling into dread as the promise comes due.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Doesn't Cry
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. The child reveals fragments: her mother is dead, Anton is her father, and men came asking questions in Dover. Orsen realizes the note's sender is watching. Beat: tenderness Orsen doesn't know how to carry.

chapters.title: Sergeant Quill Calls
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A police sergeant interviews the household about 'a German agent.' Marguerite covers for Orsen without being asked. Beat: debt and suspicion braided together.

chapters.title: What the Ice Does to a River
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite discovers Orsen's cache of letters and confronts them. Instead of betrayal, she offers help—but insists Ida must go to authorities. Beat: two moral codes colliding.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen seeks a smuggler to move Ida upriver before the freeze; the price is information about Marguerite's pacifist network. Beat: the cost of survival measured in other people's secrets.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback to the summer of 1913, when Anton visited England and the two argued about whether promises survive politics. Beat: warmth, and the reader's knowledge of what's coming.

chapters.title: The House That Stops Speaking
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida overhears the household debating her fate and runs away to the river alone. Orsen finds her at the frozen shallows. Beat: terror, and the child forcing everyone's hand.

chapters.title: Enemy Property
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite's organization expels members with German ties; her own mail is opened now, by someone else. She understands viscerally what Orsen has always done. Beat: uncomfortable empathy.

chapters.title: The Long Road to Marlow
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen drives Ida through checkpoint country disguised as a mourning errand, using a dead woman's papers. Beat: suspense; Orsen's invisibility becomes their greatest skill.

chapters.title: Quill's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The sergeant returns with a photograph of Anton and a question about the child. Orsen lies again, better, and hates it. Beat: guilt hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Ida Remembers of Her Mother
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida tells Orsen about her English mother and the night she died, revealing Anton isn't fleeing espionage but conscription and a death warrant. Beat: the enemy made human.

chapters.title: The Letter Orsen Never Sent
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen writes to Anton arranging a crossing at the weir before the river locks with ice, then burns the reply unread for the first time in their life. Beat: trust as an act of faith.

chapters.title: Marguerite Arrested
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite is detained for her pacifist pamphlets; the house empties. She entrusts Orsen with her own letter to deliver—mirroring Orsen's role. Beat: the mentor becomes the charge.

chapters.title: The Night the River Began to Close
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The smuggler betrays them to Quill; Orsen learns the crossing point is compromised hours before the rendezvous. Beat: everything collapses at once.

chapters.title: Across the Ice
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen takes Ida across the cracking river themselves at night, pursued, delivering the child to Anton on the far bank. Beat: climax—sacrifice, terror, and the promise kept.

chapters.title: The Face They Remember
chapters.summary: Anton's POV. Anton thanks Orsen and asks them to come along; Orsen refuses—Marguerite needs her letter delivered and her name defended. Beat: choosing duty over escape, love over safety.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen walks into the tribunal, reads Marguerite's letter aloud, and for the first time speaks as themselves, not a shadow. Beat: invisibility shed at last.

chapters.title: Spring Water Under Ice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, released. Marguerite and Orsen reconcile over the secrets between them; she offers Orsen a real position, not a servant's role. Beat: repair without erasure.

chapters.title: A Letter, Delivered
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A spring letter arrives from Ida; Orsen delivers it to Marguerite unopened, a new habit, and watches the thawing river. Beat: quiet hope, inheritance of a different kind.
